broad_starting_area: personal collection room and the relation between objects and display media

menu.premise: A collector of ornate house keys fits the still-dripping key from her own door into a velvet-lined miniature house; fresh radial blood droplets cross its glass roof while the real lock remains visible behind her.

A collector has opened a crowded cabinet of porcelain lapdogs after a violent splash struck its inner glass; one empty velvet footprint and the matching red trace on her home slipper suggest that the cabinet has begun collecting its owner.

In a domestic collection room, a woman holds a disconnected brass intercom receiver as its felt-lined display compartment is freshly spattered; an ordinary connected intercom in the hall has its indicator lit, joining private collecting to an intrusion.

A collector lowers a glass bell over a silver cake stand carrying a broken sugar house and blood-like splatter; behind the display sits her own intact home in a framed domestic photograph, turning decorative ownership into a threat.

A collector discovers that one ornate knob in her wall-mounted collection has rotated toward an unlatched bedroom door; fresh blood spatter fans across its cream display backing while her fingers stop at the cabinet latch.

menu.concept: The velvet drawer of compact mirrors
menu.premise: A collector slides open a velvet-lined drawer of antique powder compacts; one mirror has shattered under a fresh impact, scattering blood droplets on neighboring mother-of-pearl lids while the reflected door behind her stands newly open.
